name: Autopsy
tagline: A one-line install that records coding-agent sessions, diagnoses rejected runs and warns the agent before it repeats a mistake.
problem: Coding agents start every run from a clean slate and repeat the same mistakes, such as skipped migrations or drifted types.
solution: Records every opencode event into Postgres, classifies rejected runs with deterministic rules, builds a failure graph with vector embeddings and serves a preflight retrieval step to the next run.
demo_moment: Team-described: an agent run is rejected, Autopsy explains why, and the next run avoids the mistake.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won “3rd Overall” and “Cognition Company Challenge” among 307 submissions.
Turns an agent's rejected runs into memory it consults before the next run.
About 165 tests sit behind the one-line installer.

lessons: Give agents a feedback loop from their own failures; judges who use agents recognise the pain at once.
